## What this dashboard shows

- This dashboard tracks cost center spend across Wipro Enterprises, covering 160 active cost centers that collectively account for ₹1,217.66B in total expenses.
- Total expenses increased +28.7% last month, with an average spend of ₹5.36B per cost center.
- The data spans multiple business units (Consumer Care & Lighting, Infrastructure Engineering, Joint Ventures) and is sourced from both real SAP BDC systems and simulated data from SAP S/4HANA, Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and Tally Prime.

## What to report

- Total assigned cost center spend reached ₹1,217.66B, up +28.7% month-on-month, with 160 active cost centers averaging ₹5.36B each.
- Manufacturing dominates spend: cost center "200 Manufacturing" leads at ₹137.40B in FY2025, followed by "MFG Manufacturing" at ₹89.79B and "Factory Factory" at ₹65.86B.
- SG&A overhead represents 31.8% of total spend, with Management & Administration at 14.7%; production and supply chain centers account for only 2.4% of spend.
- Sales, Administration, and Marketing cost centers (100, 300, 400) collectively represent ₹29.85B, ₹28.77B, and ₹18.86B respectively in FY2025, indicating significant commercial and overhead investment.

## Watch out for

- Multiple cost centers show large negative balances in FY2026, notably F1US1201 Purch & Store 1 (US) at -₹21.94B and several product line centers ranging from -₹1.04B to -₹6.88B, suggesting reversal entries, accrual adjustments, or data quality issues requiring investigation.
- Production-related cost centers account for only 2.4% of total spend despite manufacturing centers topping the expense list—confirm whether production departments are correctly classified or if direct material costs sit outside cost center assignment.
- Data includes "Simulated SAP" and "Simulated SAP S/4HANA" source systems; verify which portions of the ₹1,217.66B total are simulated vs. actual, as this affects reliability for board reporting.
- The Total Expenses figure is stated to be lower than the Overview dashboard total because it excludes unassigned spend lines—request the variance amount to understand the completeness of cost center coverage.
